This is a bake-off: the same brief runs for three characters and the owner compares the rendered tests.

The bible rule must land inside 12 seconds; the signature gesture may be used once.
Any dance or move is original and fully described; no trending dance or sound.

No readable brand text in frame.
No real people or recognisable locations.

premises.logline: At a busy junction Captain Tempo conducts the red-man countdown for a blurred stream of pedestrians, shouts THREE, TWO, ONE, AND, the signal flips exactly when it was always going to, she detonates the Tempo Stomp, and a commuter walks straight through her fist-pump without a glance while the camera holds one beat too long.
premises.audience_emotion: Delighted disbelief, then warm laughter at pure misplaced confidence.
premises.character_desire: To make the whole city move in time, starting with this crossing.
premises.obstacle: The signal runs on its own timer and the crowd is indifferent to her.
premises.escalation: Low-angle push-in as the count drops from a whisper-shout to a roar; arms conduct harder each number; the whistle joins on TWO.
premises.surprise: The Stomp lands, and a passer-by calmly walks through the middle of her celebration, hair-width from her raised fists, never looking over.
premises.payoff: Bible rule in full: she counts down aloud with her whole body, the light changes on its own schedule, she celebrates with the original Tempo Stomp (two stomps, hip swing, whistle blast, both fists to the sky) as if she caused it, a passer-by walks through it unnoticing, and the camera lingers one beat too long on her frozen victory pose.
premises.structure: Setup-countdown-release-deflation: one continuous build to a single beat, then a held anticlimax.
premises.why_send_it: Anyone who has ever stood at a crossing and felt personally responsible for the light sends it to the friend who 'always makes the green come'.

production_format.camera_style: Handheld phone, wide, slow low-angle push-in from across the road toward her; the camera is the crowd's indifferent witness, settling on a held beat after the Stomp.
production_format.rationale: Clearest single-take introduction of energy, rule and silhouette; a push-in sells her towering scale, one unit and zero cuts fit draft_mini, and shouted numbers are universal when muted. It is the bible's canonical location so the rule is unambiguous.

premises.logline: In a glass shopping-centre lift lobby, Captain Tempo silently conducts the lift down from the top floor with finger counts and whistle blasts; it arrives, she celebrates, the doors open on nobody, she steps in and the clip ends on the exact opening frame so it replays as if the lift had just been summoned again.
premises.audience_emotion: Hypnotic, absurd satisfaction; a calm loop-laugh.
premises.character_desire: To bring the lift down on the beat.
premises.obstacle: Floors descend at lift speed; she cannot hurry them and will not stop conducting.
premises.escalation: Floor indicator lights tick down while her gestures grow from baton-small to full-arm sweeps; the whistle punctuates each floor.
premises.surprise: The doors open and the lift is empty and has plainly been coming all along; the final frame silently mirrors frame one, restarting the whole gag.
premises.payoff: Visible displacement: she credits herself for an arrival that was always going to happen, then the loop resets her to the same hopeful pose. The Tempo Stomp fires once on arrival while a blurred shopper crosses behind the glass without turning.
premises.structure: Loop: ending frame equals opening frame so the countdown reads as endless.
premises.why_send_it: Loop-watchers send it to a colleague who also 'calls' the lift by pressing the button three extra times.
premises.commercial_fit: None; keep signage out of frame.
premises.rejected_because: loop gimmick dilutes the spoken counting that carries the bible voice; lift floor display is small to read muted

production_format.camera_style: Locked-off phone at a slight low angle in front of the glass lift; she fills the left third, floor lights and moving lift cage give the frame its clock.
production_format.rationale: Tests a quieter register than P1: the count lives in fingers, whistle foley and the lift lights, so legibility muted is proven; a loop ending suits autoplay. The location is new to show range, the costume unchanged because the silhouette is fixed.

premises.logline: Captain Tempo, filming herself at arm's length in a bakery queue, counts down the number display to her turn; a deadpan voice off camera keeps confirming each number; when her number lands she celebrates, and the baker serves the next blurred customer behind her without a glance.
premises.audience_emotion: Affectionate, intimate amusement, as if she is a loud friend vlogging a tiny triumph.
premises.character_desire: To get her loaf on the beat she herself called.
premises.obstacle: The queue moves at its own pace and the numbers advance by someone else's rhythm.
premises.escalation: Her selfie view tilts as she bounces on her toes; each tick brings her closer to the lens until her eyebrows fill the frame.
premises.surprise: Her number turns out to be called while she is mid-Stomp, so the Stomp becomes the answer to a question nobody asked; the off-camera voice flatly says 'Your loaf.'
premises.payoff: Bible rule in full: she counts the queue down aloud, it resolves on its own schedule, she celebrates with the Tempo Stomp as if she caused it, and a customer walks through her celebration unnoticing while the phone lingers one beat too long.
premises.structure: Vlog-style countdown to a mundane payoff, closed by a second voice puncturing it.
premises.why_send_it: People send it to a sibling who narrates the queue like a sport.
premises.commercial_fit: None; no real products or brand names.
premises.rejected_because: phone-in-hand framing loses her full-body silhouette and the Stomp; bakery interior risks readable text

production_format.camera_style: Phone held by Captain Tempo at arm's length, wobbling with her bounce, then dropping to waist height for the Stomp so her whole teal-and-gold figure is visible.
production_format.rationale: Shows the character from her own point of view, which proves the identity anchors hold when she is close to the lens; the off-camera voice allows a second, flat comic rhythm while keeping one on-camera speaker.

premises.logline: At a crossing, a clipped metronome on Captain Tempo's waistband ticks in sync with a bus she is counting in; one insert close-up of the metronome shows its arm stop dead the instant the bus arrives, and she turns to face camera and Stomps as if she stopped it.
premises.audience_emotion: Playful curiosity, then a small rush of rhythm-satisfaction.
premises.character_desire: To bring the bus in on tempo.
premises.obstacle: A bus does not obey a metronome; it arrives when it arrives.
premises.escalation: Wide shot: her conducting widens as the bus nears in the background; a single cut to the metronome close-up shows its swing slowing and her thumb nudging it.
premises.surprise: The metronome's stop and the bus's arrival land together only because she nudged the arm, so she is both cause and fraud.
premises.payoff: A cheap lie rewarded: the bus arrives on its own, the Tempo Stomp lands, a blurred commuter boards without noticing, and the final shot lingers one beat too long.
premises.structure: Wide-insert-wide: main action, one cutaway detail that reframes it, then a return to the celebration.
premises.why_send_it: For the friend who 'times' their arrival to match the bus and takes the credit.
premises.commercial_fit: None; no readable bus or route text.
premises.rejected_because: the single insert spends the entire cut budget on a prop gag; the Stomp competes with the insert for the clip's beats

production_format.camera_style: Wide locked-off phone with a slight low angle, plus one macro insert of the waist metronome assembled in edit; the single hard cut is the only edit.
production_format.rationale: A one-cut architecture that fits draft_mini; text-only audio tests whether the idea reads on mute, with a post-added counter (3, 2, 1) since there is no speech.

premises.logline: In the lift lobby Captain Tempo counts a lift down from five, but it arrives on THREE; undaunted, she restarts and counts it back up to a celebration, claiming a victory she visibly miscounted, while the blurred crowd steps around her.
premises.character_desire: To be the reason the lift came when she said it would.
premises.obstacle: The lift is early, which ruins her count and threatens her authority.
premises.escalation: The count races to reconcile the lift's early arrival; her volume rises through the restart; the whistle blasts twice in disbelief.
premises.surprise: She does not admit the miss: she runs the count back up to meet the lift and Stomps anyway, bending reality to her tempo.
premises.payoff: Failure reframed as victory: the Tempo Stomp lands over a doors-already-open lift, and the camera holds a beat too long on her glowing, wrong, perfectly happy face.
premises.structure: Reversal: expectation set, expectation broken, character bends the world's schedule to her own story.
premises.why_send_it: For the friend who never admits being wrong and claims credit anyway.
premises.commercial_fit: None; keep lift panels and signs unreadable.
premises.rejected_because: the miscount undercuts the bible rule that it always happens on its own schedule, and muting it is slightly harder to read

production_format.camera_style: Locked-off phone, wide, slightly low angle on a tripod-height prop in front of the glass lift so she fills the frame with the lift doors behind her.
production_format.rationale: A static single take is the cheapest render and a deliberate contrast to P1's moving camera; a new location shows range while the same voice keeps the counting hook recognisable.

hook_variants.first_frame: Handheld phone, wide and slightly low across a busy junction: Captain Tempo in glossy teal and gold tracksuit, white sweatband, red-cord whistle, chunky white trainers, stands at the kerb towering over a blurred grey stream of pedestrians, both arms raised like a conductor about to cue the orchestra, the red standing-man signal glowing behind her (no readable text).
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: Her raised arms slam down on the beat as she bellows 'THREE!' and the camera starts its slow push-in.
hook_variants.rationale: Silhouette, scale, public setting and the conducting posture read in one second muted, and the downbeat promises a countdown with a payoff; it is the cleanest send-to-the-friend-who-thinks-they-control-the-light hook.

hook_variants.first_frame: Extreme low-angle close frame on the small metronome clipped to her glossy teal waistband, its arm ticking left and right in sharp focus, the red crossing signal and blurred legs of passers-by soft behind it.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: Without a cut the phone tilts up the tracksuit zip to her gap-toothed grin as she whistle-blasts once and shouts 'TWO!'.
hook_variants.rationale: The ticking prop is a vivid, specific tease and the tilt-up reveals the character, but the first frame alone does not show her silhouette or the crossing clearly enough to hit full legibility.

hook_variants.first_frame: Wide low-angle shot from the far kerb: Captain Tempo stands with her back half to camera, facing the blurred crowd gathered at the crossing the way a conductor faces an orchestra, fists clenched at chest height, whistle in her teeth, saturated teal and gold against grey tarmac.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: She blasts the whistle and flings her arms wide in a huge cue; the stream of pedestrians simply keeps walking, unaffected, as she hisses 'AND...' under her breath.
hook_variants.rationale: A tiny woman commanding an indifferent crowd shows the bible's core contradiction instantly and reads muted, though the setup arrives slightly before the countdown so the rule is promised a beat later than in H1.

hook_variants.first_frame: Selfie-view at arm's length, wobbling: Captain Tempo's lean weathered face, wide grey eyes and raised silver-spiky hair fill the frame, her eyebrows arched mid-bounce, a blurred bakery queue and an unlabelled glowing number display behind her shoulder.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: She jabs a finger at the number display behind her and stage-whispers 'FOUR...' with huge eyebrow work straight to lens.
hook_variants.rationale: The face, eyebrows and a very legible small problem (waiting for your number) read muted and feel intimate, though the full silhouette is not yet visible, which costs a point on legibility.

hook_variants.first_frame: Selfie-view at arm's length: Captain Tempo, mid-sentence, leans toward the lens and points her whole arm directly at the viewer, the blurred bakery queue behind, her sweatband and whistle cord visible at the frame edge.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: She mouths and hisses 'YOU. Hold my place. THREE...' then swings the phone round to the queue and begins counting down with a finger.
hook_variants.rationale: Directly addressing the viewer makes it highly sendable and the countdown starts at once, but the command is spoken so it reads weaker muted and the pointing gesture is generic rather than specific to her.

hook_variants.first_frame: Phone dropped to waist height so her whole teal-and-gold figure bounces on tiptoe in the foreground, arms half raised, chunky white trainers visible, the blurred bakery queue shuffling forward behind her.
hook_variants.first_line_or_action: A flat off-camera voice says 'Forty-one.' and she answers by throwing both arms up and shouting 'COMING IN ON THE BEAT!'.
hook_variants.rationale: The full silhouette is strong and anyone who narrates a queue will recognise the mood, but the deadpan voice is audio-dependent and the rule does not appear in the first second.

selected.rationale: P1 with H1 shows the full silhouette, public setting, conducting body language and a countdown promise in the first frame, so energy, rule and silhouette are legible muted, and its single-take moving-camera plus on-camera-dialogue pair is not in the recent list (empty) and fits one draft_mini unit with zero cuts. The trade-off against the runner-up (P3 with H4) is that P3 is more intimate and tests close-range identity anchors, but it loses her full-body silhouette and the Tempo Stomp and risks readable bakery text, so P1 is the safer cold introduction.

script.title: Captain Tempo Counts the Crossing
script.synopsis: At a busy junction Captain Tempo counts down THREE, TWO, ONE, AND with her whole body; the signal flips on its own timer; she erupts into the Tempo Stomp as if she caused it; a commuter walks through her celebration without a glance and the camera lingers one beat too long.

beats.beat: Wide low shot: towering teal-and-gold woman, arms raised like a conductor, red figure glowing; downbeat on THREE
Conducting arms and bounce build; the countdown is the rule stated aloud
Whistle blast on TWO, roar of ONE, push-in tightens
AND: the signal flips on its own timer; Tempo Stomp
Commuter walks through her frozen victory; camera lingers one beat too long

script.caption_text: She counted. The light changed. Obviously she did that.
